Chapter 204: President Chen is Taking His Final Exams

"Bang, bang, bang!"

"Pass the ball, pass the ball!"

"Damn it, get back on defense."

On the basketball court at Peking University, Chen Guiliang was working up a sweat.

When he had just been reborn, his body was weak from malnutrition, so he used to work out diligently every day. Since starting university, he had been swamped with work all day and had no time to exercise at all.

A few days ago, after watching an NBA highlight reel, Chen Guiliang finally decided to get more active.

He even decided to organize a basketball game in the spring: ByteDance vs. Game Science.

He wanted to let his employees stretch their legs a bit too.

"Hah... hah... hah..."

After running for more than ten minutes, Xie Yang was already bent over, hands on his knees, panting heavily.

"Xie Saobang, you need to exercise more," Chen Guiliang said with a laugh.

Xie Yang was dizzy. "Don't... don't want to talk."

Guo Feng played basketball like a complete gentleman. The guy strolled around the whole time, acting like an old man.

On the other hand, Dong Qianqiu, who was under 1.7 meters tall, was dashing all over the court with his glasses on, and his dribbling skills were very slick.

"Pass!" Yang Shuo yelled.

Dong Qianqiu didn't pass immediately. Instead, he used a series of fakes, dribbling left and right. After shaking off his opponent, he suddenly threw the ball to the corner.

Yang Shuo jumped to catch the ball and, relying on the physique he had built in the army, forced his way towards the basket.

"Clang!"

He scored with a hook shot.

Dong Qianqiu ran over and high-fived Yang Shuo to celebrate.

A male student from Peking University's materials science department, sitting on the ground, raised his hand and shouted, "He charged. That's a foul, a foul!"

Yang Shuo retorted, "You were blocking."

It was a pickup game, so of course, there was no referee.

Chen Guiliang walked over with a smile and reached out to pull the student up. "Alright, alright, we can't settle this anyway. I'll treat everyone to a meal after the game."

"Fine, I'll give President Chen some face."

The student didn't say anything more and picked up the basketball to inbound it.

Another half hour passed. Chen Guiliang sat on the sideline wiping his sweat. He was soaked through and exhausted, but the feeling of exercising was incredibly refreshing.

Players from both teams were now sitting on the sideline, drinking the Red Bull that President Chen had bought for everyone.

A student asked Yang Shuo, "Bro, are you on the school team?"

Yang Shuo, who was fierce on the court, now looked simple and honest, grinning as he said, "I played a lot when I was in the army. The troops had basketball competitions too."

"A veteran?"

"Yeah."

"My respects."

"There are a lot of veterans, but not many Peking University students. Sorry about earlier, I knocked you over twice. My skills are a bit rough, and I tend to run into people when I'm on offense."

"It's just basketball, physical contact is normal."

After six months at the company, Yang Shuo was getting better and better at making small talk.

Chen Guiliang patted his pants and stood up. "Let's go, let's get some skewers."

In the dead of winter, the weather was too cold, so getting skewers turned into having hot pot.

A few bites of sliced lamb, and everyone instantly felt warm all over. Those who knew each other and those who didn't clinked glasses and shot the breeze.

Halfway through the meal, Qu Guohao called. "The final four for the Legends of the Three Kingdoms University League are out. Xi'an Jiaotong, Shandong University, Sichuan University, and South China University of Technology."

Chen Guiliang laughed. "The universities in Beijing and Shanghai aren't doing so well, not a single one in the final four."

The first Legends of the Three Kingdoms National University League had started its open qualifiers during the National Day holiday, and the subsequent round-robin and knockout stages were all held online on weekends.

After the final four were decided, it was time for the offline matches, scheduled for winter break.

The venue had been decided: the Peking University Hall. It required a 15,000 yuan fee to Peking University for venue and equipment rental.

Additionally, the Peking University cafeteria would provide the meals.

Depending on the seating, ticket prices ranged from 15 to 30 yuan, which also included a cafeteria lunch. There would be small gifts as well.

It was purely a loss-leader to generate buzz.

The event would be recorded for broadcast by GameFY and live-streamed with text and pictures on Xiaonei and 17173.

Qu Guohao added, "This afternoon, SOHU-IT sent an electronic invitation. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* has been nominated for '2005 Best Domestically Produced Online Game' and '2005 Best Historical Online Game.' Someone needs to go accept the award in person."

"Where is the award ceremony?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qu Guohao said, "It's very close. Just a few kilometers south from the east gate of Peking University. But on the day of the ceremony, President Chen, I think you have final exams..."

Chen Guiliang, holding his phone, asked Dong Qianqiu who was busy cooking lamb slices, "Old Dong, *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was originally developed by you and Guo Feng. Do you want to go accept the award?"

"Is it far?" Dong Qianqiu asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's only a few kilometers from the east gate of Peking University."

Dong Qianqiu nodded. "Sure, I'll go then."

Chen Guiliang raised his phone and told Qu Guohao, "Engineer Dong will go accept the award."

After a few more words, he hung up.

Xiaonei and Kaixin had won quite a few awards, and *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was not to be outdone.

But the timing of the gaming award ceremonies was awkward, with most of them concentrated during Chen Guiliang's final exams.

The most authoritative of these was the "China Game Industry Annual Conference and Award Ceremony," an event hosted by the GAPP. Representatives from ten national ministries and commissions would be in attendance, along with over 200 game companies from mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.

If it were held in Beijing, Chen Guiliang could have rushed over after his exams, but the problem was the venue was far away in Xiamen.

Chen Guiliang naturally chose to dutifully take his exams.

Dong Qianqiu was only willing to attend events in Beijing; Xiamen was too far, and he couldn't be bothered to go.

So Qu Guohao had to fly over.

Someone had to attend, and they had to be careful. After all, this event was hosted by the GAPP with personnel from ten national ministries in attendance. Offending any one of them would make things impossible.

Arriving at the Xiamen venue, Qu Guohao was filled with emotion.

He had worked at Etang for several years, and although his position had steadily risen, he ended up getting laid off. He was already at home preparing for the postgraduate entrance exams when Chen Guiliang showed up at his door with an invitation, and now he had even made him the general manager of Game Science.

It all felt like a dream.

Fortunately, Game Science's early management staff were all currently at ByteDance. The first batch of new hires later on were also those left over after ByteDance's selection.

In terms of ability and industry experience, Qu Guohao could just barely command the respect of his subordinates, with the exception of Dong Qianqiu.

Fortunately, Dong Qianqiu only cared about technology and wasn't interested in other matters.

Entering the conference hall, Qu Guohao saw many bigwigs, as well as countless game companies whose names he didn't recognize.

The first morning was filled with speeches from leaders of various levels and big shots from the gaming world.

Among them, the "2005 China Game Industry Annual Report," disclosed for the first time at the event, caught the attention of everyone in the industry: "By the end of 2005, the number of online game users in China has reached 26.34 million. The number of paying users is 13.51 million, an increase of over 30% from the same period last year... In 2005, online game sales revenue reached 3.77 billion yuan..."

In the afternoon, Qu Guohao attended a forum and bluffed his way through a speech he had prepared.

That night, Qu Guohao sent a text to Chen Guiliang: "I just went on stage."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What did you say?"

Qu Guohao replied, "I sang."

"You sang?"

"Yeah. Tonight's event was called 'King of KTV.' Industry elites from the gaming world went on stage to sing. It was sort of like a gala for the game industry. Sohu's Charles Zhang was the first to go on and sing, and Shanda's Tang Jun sang a song too..."

Reading the text message, Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

He really wanted to be there in person to film those guys singing. Ten years from now, he could post it online. It would be a treasure trove of embarrassing history.

The award ceremony itself was not held until the next afternoon.

There were two hosts, a man and a woman.

The male host was CCTV's Li Yong, and the female host was Xiamen TV's Chen Ling.

The first award was the Game Industry Support Award, presented to local governments that supported the development of the game industry.

For the second award, Li Yong said, "We will now present the 2005 China Game Enterprise Rising Star Award. The winning companies are..."
